newsitem.title: UK: Excerpts from UK Chancellor Clarke's speech.
newsitem.headline: Excerpts from UK Chancellor Clarke's speech.

text.p: Following are excerpts from the prepared text of Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's speech to the Conservative party conference in Bournemouth:
- Clarke described the Conservative party as being "tax-cutters by instinct and action".

- "We will keep borrowing coming down. We will ensure tight control of spending, while properly funding our key services. And when I have done those things, and only then, I will assess the room for any tax cuts this November. As I said to conference last year -- and I say it again -- for Conservatives, tax cuts must be for keeps."
- "My Budget this year will not just be set with a few months in mind. We all have many years in mind. We are going to govern much longer than the next few months."

- "We must create the climate for continued Conservative economic success over the next five years. And my Budget in November must create the climate for an honest election campaign in which we play fair and straight with the public - and win five more years."
- "If we fight the election on the economy, we will win. And with a Tory government back in power, the economy will do even better."
- "We will cut the basic rate of income tax to 20p in the pound. Already a quarter of all taxpayers only pay tax at 20p, eventually 20p will be the basic rate for everyone."
- Clarke promised to reduce and then abolish inheritance and capital gains tax and get public spending down below 40% of GDP.
- Clarke said all Conservatives believed in low taxes. The debate was not about whether to cut them, but when and how.

- "I said on television 10 days ago that the people would not trust us if we tried to buy the next election by unsustainable tax cuts. It was a statement of the truth -- the bald and obvious truth. To earn and keep the trust of the British people, we have to follow one Tory golden rule. We only cut taxes when we can afford to and when it is good for the economy. That is the rule we must follow in this Parliament, and in the next Parliament, and in every Parliament in which the Conservatives will hold power."
- "Affordable tax cuts are food for the economy. Unaffordable tax cuts can only damage the economy."

- Clarke said the key to tax cuts was the control of public spending and reduction of public borrowing. Tax would be a big issue in the election, but the question people would ask was not who had cut taxes in any one year, but who would cut them over many years."
- "Who on earth believes they will pay lower taxes if they elect a Labour government? Anyone who believes that will believe I am following Nigel Lawson's diet plan."
- Clarke said tough decisions had been taken to produce the best economic conditions in a lifetime. People could see it in more jobs, more cars, busier shops and more people moving home.

- "Now they can feel the benefits of Tory economic policy as never before. Real incomes in Britain have never been higher. The average family will be 700 stg better off this year, after inflation and after tax, than at the time of the last election."
- Clarke said that with the longest run of low inflation for 50 years, the lowest mortgage rates for 30 years, Britain was leading the European economy as never before.
- Attacking opposition Labour party shadow chancellor Gordon Brown, he said:
- "Gordon Brown bases his policies on the Dolly Parton school of economics: an unbelievable figure, blown out of all proportion, with no visible means of support."

- Clarke said that while the Conservative instinct was to spend less and tax less, while keeping borrowing down to a minimum, Labour's instinct was the opposite. "To live for the short term, to spend before you earn, to run up debts and put up taxes, your taxes, to pay the bill. They have all been trained in the Robert Maxwell school of creative accounting."
- "The idea of Labour backing business, keeping taxes low and reducing the deficit is completely absurd. It isn't just a matter of pigs flying. It's a whole farmyard on a mission deep into space.

- "I say this to the public. Do not trust Tony Blair. Do not buy a used car from this man. Do not be deceived by Gordon Brown. Do not buy a new car from this man. They will not come clean with you. You should not place your votes into their long-fingered hands and their slippery palms. They will wreck our enterprise economy. They will squander our prospects. They will spoil our economic success."
- Promising to cut taxes, control public spending and keep inflation down, Clarke said: "These are our guiding stars -- enterprise, incentives, opportunity for all."
-- London Newsroom 44 171 542 2774
